{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZTPCIg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC6X6s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 19, "title": "Implement BG3 offset-per-tile addressing for background Modes 2 and 4", "body": "## Problem

Modes 2 and 4 currently render BG1/BG2 with ordinary scrolling, ignoring BG3 offset-table words. This omits a standard background-addressing mechanism even though the planar tile renderer, scroll registers and tilemap storage already exist.

At baseline `c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c`, [`Ppu::bg_pixel`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L274-L325) selects Mode 2/4 pixel depths but derives source coordinates solely from each background's ordinary scroll values. There is no BG3 offset-table lookup. Implementing this addressing step is a bounded addition to the existing renderer and a foundation for eventual Mode 6 support.

## Expected outcome

Implement non-mosaic Mode 2/4 offset-per-tile addressing for BG1 and BG2 within the existing scanline renderer.

### Hardware semantics

Use [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), specifically its Mode 2/4/6 offset-per-tile description and BGMODE, BG3SC, BG3HOFS and BG3VOFS register descriptions. Fullsnes is already a repository hardware reference in [`docs/issue-5-validation.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/docs/issue-5-validation.md#L65-L76).

- BG3 supplies offset words rather than a visible third background. Its TM/TS enable bits must not gate offset-table operation.
- Offset-word bit 13 enables replacement for BG1; bit 14 enables replacement for BG2. Disabled replacements retain the affected background's ordinary scroll on that axis.
- Mode 2 obtains independent horizontal and vertical words from BG3 table coordinates selected by BG3VOFS and BG3VOFS + 8. Table-row selection does not advance with the displayed scanline.
- Mode 4 uses one word. Bit 15 selects horizontal replacement when clear and vertical replacement when set. It does not obtain an independent vertical replacement from the following row.
- Horizontal replacement preserves the affected background's ordinary three-bit fine scroll. Offset-word bits 0–2 do not replace those fine bits. Vertical replacement uses the word's ten-bit offset and replaces ordinary vertical scroll; it is not added to that scroll.
- With screen coordinate `x`, define `q = x + (BGnHOFS & 7)`. While `q < 8`, use ordinary scrolling. Otherwise the offset-table horizontal coordinate is `q - 8 + (BG3HOFS & ~7)`. Thus the initial unaffected region depends on the affected background's fine scroll, and BG3's horizontal fine bits do not shift table selection.
- For an enabled horizontal replacement `H`, source X is `(x + (BGnHOFS & 7) + (H & 0x3f8)) & 0x3ff`. For an enabled vertical replacement `V`, source Y is `(s + (V & 0x3ff)) & 0x3ff`, where `s` is the background scanline coordinate; the current renderer uses `y + 1`.
- Resolve table words through the documented BG3 screen-base, screen-size, tile-size and scroll addressing, including page boundaries and VRAM wrapping. Treat words as offset descriptors rather than applying ordinary tile palette, priority or flip interpretation.
- Feed the resulting coordinates into existing tile selection, flips, transparency, priority, main/subscreen composition and Mode 4 direct color. Offset-column selection must remain distinct from the affected background's 8×8/16×16 tile selection.

Record the specification sections and independently derived addressing vectors in the implementation's validation record.

### Scope and remaining work

Include both backgrounds, both affected-background tile sizes, BG3 table addressing, register-controlled selection, and ordinary-scroll fallback. Keep the existing output dimensions and scanline snapshot model.

Mode 6 remains unimplemented: it also needs hires geometry and its mode-specific addressing. Mosaic/offset interactions, timed mosaic state, mid-scanline register changes and fetch timing remain outside this Issue and must remain explicitly unverified. Do not imply that completing this Issue completes `ppu-offset`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-hires` or `ppu-raster`. Preserve the scope and evidence of every other inventory category.

## Context and reproduction

1. Construct a Mode 2 scene with distinguishable source tile columns/rows, ordinary BG1 scroll and a separate BG3 offset table.
2. Set bit 13 in a horizontal offset word and choose a replacement coarse scroll different from ordinary BG1 scrolling.
3. Render across the first eligible offset-column boundary. Expected: the initial region retains ordinary scrolling, followed by pixels from the replacement source column. Current code continues ordinary scrolling throughout.
4. Repeat with vertical replacement and with Mode 4's bit-15 selector, including BG2-only enable words.

Existing [`direct_color.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/crates/snes-core/tests/direct_color.rs#L208-L328) provides an original CPU-executed guest-builder pattern, including Mode 4. It does not test offset words. [`regression.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L644-L699) covers ordinary 16×16 subtile wrapping/flips; [`tools/ppu-test.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/tools/ppu-test.py) checks HDMA grayscale bands. Neither establishes offset-per-tile behavior.

The supplied context lists no open Issues, and recent improvements cover direct color and DSP behavior, not offset-table addressing. This evaluation inspected repository source and tests only; it made no changes, fetched no external specification pages and executed no tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the addressing behavior above without game-specific exceptions or an unrelated renderer redesign.
- [ ] Add `crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_offset.rs` with literal or independently derived source-coordinate/RGBA expectations. Demonstrate offset-enabled assertions fail against the baseline implementation and pass after the change; disabled-offset controls must pass on both.
- [ ] Cover Mode 2 horizontal-only, vertical-only and simultaneous replacements; Mode 4 horizontal/vertical selection and ignored second-row data; BG1-only, BG2-only, both and neither enable masks; and unused-bit isolation.
- [ ] Cover all eight affected-background horizontal fine-scroll values, the first eligible boundary and successive columns. Vary BG3HOFS coarse/fine bits, BG3VOFS and displayed scanline independently. Include ten-bit source-coordinate wrapping, all four BG3SC screen layouts, page crossings, VRAM wrapping and documented BG3 tile-size behavior.
- [ ] Cover affected-background 8×8 and 16×16 tiles, flips and transparent pixels. Include a Mode 4 direct-color case and main/subscreen selection. Confirm offset lookup works while BG3 is disabled in TM/TS.
- [ ] Add bounded original MIT 65C816 guests for both Modes 2 and 4, generated from source in memory. Guests must initialize registers, VRAM and CGRAM through emulated CPU writes, then produce independently expected framebuffer pixels without host-side PPU patching. Exercise enabled and disabled controls. Record source/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Pass `cargo test -p snes-core --test ppu_offset --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Preserve existing expectations, including direct-color and game-derived regressions.
- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware gates documented in [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c7ff61b9c927fe283ef1a4f753c1075d5b8f237c/README.md#validate): `python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc`, then `python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"`, and `python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"`. Retain pinned sources, licenses, fixture alterations and numerical assertions.
- [ ] Preserve browser/game gates: rebuild and compare the original smoke fixture; run `python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py` twice after tool setup; run `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, then from `web`, `npx playwright install chromium` and `npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Pass cleared Castle/Memory replays, Castle's complete route, Memory audio/effects and diagnostic/Pages tests without weakening their assertions. Only the already excluded unaudited optional games may remain excluded.
- [ ] Update README limits and add a validation record reporting commands, actual results, baseline failures, specification derivations and remaining gaps. Passing these bounded tests must not be described as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility. Planning alone changes no inventory status.

## Optional validation

None required beyond the pre-merge criteria. No commercial-game acquisition or subjective approval is needed.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
